claims.text: Sub-5 nm AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles can be synthesized by pulsed laser deposition on a silicon nitride membrane.
The as-synthesized AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles are nominally compositionally homogeneous.
The as-synthesized AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles have an FCC structure.
More than 50% of the atoms or volume-associated contribution in sub-5 nm particles is at the surface.
Surface-energy minimization dominates bulk mixing entropy in sub-5 nm AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Au and Cu have sufficiently low surface energies to segregate preferentially to the surfaces of AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles.
Surface-segregated Au and Cu evaporate from the heated nanoparticles.
Reduced atomic coordination at nanoparticle surfaces makes the surface-diffusion activation energy lower than the bulk-diffusion barrier.
Above a critical temperature, rapid surface diffusion bypasses the sluggish bulk diffusion expected in quinary high-entropy alloys.
Au/Cu surface diffusion creates a concentration gradient that produces core-shell segregation.
The proposed surface-diffusion and evaporation mechanism promotes particle coalescence.
The critical temperature for accelerated Au/Cu segregation in sub-5 nm particles lies between 600 K and 800 K.
Crossing the critical temperature causes a nonlinear acceleration of Au/Cu surface segregation.
Heating above the critical temperature causes rapid particle shrinkage and a transition from elliptical or icosahedral shapes to spherical shapes.
Initially icosahedral particles segregate faster than truncated octahedral particles because icosahedra have higher surface energy.
Surface-energy dominance applies only below 10 nm, whereas particles larger than 20 nm recover bulk-entropy-dominated sluggish diffusion.
Sluggish diffusion has been reported in high-entropy alloys and associated with elevated diffusion activation energies and enhanced stability.
High entropy and sluggish diffusion would prevent segregation and preserve AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticle size and shape up to the bulk melting point.

contradictions.description: The initial-state field describes elliptical or icosahedral particles, while the conditions and shape-dependent prediction require truncated octahedral particles as part of the initial population. The intended initial shape classes are therefore inconsistent or incompletely specified.

The design says surface-diffusion barriers will be artificially suppressed, which normally means lowering barriers and enhancing diffusion, but then describes this as removing surface effects. The measurements and falsification rule instead refer to surface diffusion being constrained or suppressed, meaning reduced diffusion. These are opposite simulation interventions.
